parts.note: EP is an extended-play record

indicators.note: not finishing means the last letter of the word for several is dropped

parts.note: some means several, an unspecified few

explanation.surface: A race record set where several runners fail to complete the course.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsom Downs is an English racecourse, home of the Derby, so it is a horse-racing course.

clue.text: Put flowers around a river in this demi-paradise?

indicators.note: the article and the river's abbreviation go inside the country

parts.note: Shakespeare's Richard II calls England 'this other Eden, demi-paradise'

explanation.surface: Decorating a river with flowers in an idyllic land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this demi-paradise' quotes John of Gaunt's speech in Shakespeare's Richard II praising England.
explanation.definitionFit: To engarland is to adorn with a wreath or garland, decking with blooms.

indicators.note: the troublesome letters will not behave and fall into a new order

explanation.surface: An uncle named Rod has a sore heel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troublesome' rearranges UNCLE RODS; 'heel' looks like part of a foot but means a cad.
explanation.definitionFit: A heel is a contemptible, dishonourable person, a rogue or cad.

indicators.note: the chaps hug the numeral between them

parts.note: chaps are men
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: The way men behave when hugging someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Mien is a person's bearing or demeanour, the way they carry themselves.

parts.note: split the first word: a type of cape (a sleeveless overcoat) that shares its name with a Highland town

explanation.surface: A geography slip, placing the South African city in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: Cape Town tempts you towards South Africa; read it as cape + town. An Inverness cape is a sleeveless coat with a cape, and Inverness is the main town of the Scottish Highlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a garment style (the Inverness cape) and a Highland town carry this name.

parts.note: read taking in as eating and workers as worker ants or bees: a creature that dines on bugs

explanation.surface: A firm hiring staff as an illustration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'workers' suggests employees; in crosswords it often means ants or bees, and 'taking in' means eating.
explanation.definitionFit: Insectivorous creatures feed on bugs, such as worker ants and bees.

clue.text: Humdrum existence at hospital for a girl?

parts.note: a rut is a dull, unvarying routine

explanation.surface: A dull life in a hospital, for a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruth is a female first name.

parts.note: a quip is a witty remark

explanation.surface: A standard English joke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stock' looks like an adjective (stock joke); it is the verb meaning supply.
explanation.definitionFit: To stock a place is to supply or furnish it with what is needed.

clue.text: This girl is lazy, taking a turn at table

definitions.text: This girl is lazy, taking a turn at table

parts.words: This girl is lazy, taking a turn at table
parts.note: a woman's name that, with the word lazy before it, names a revolving tray on a dining table

explanation.surface: An idle young woman takes her turn serving at dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: A lazy Susan is a rotating tray in the middle of a table; 'taking a turn' is the spin.
explanation.definitionFit: Lazy Susan is the name for a revolving serving stand placed at the table's centre.

parts.note: a famous Shakespearean playhouse whose name also means a sphere, something perfectly round

explanation.surface: A staging format where the audience surrounds the actors.
explanation.walkthrough: The Globe was Shakespeare's playhouse on London's South Bank, and a globe is itself a round object.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Globe was a circular playhouse, and its name is a word for a sphere.

clue.text: True cases opened to reveal pruner's equipment

indicators.note: the words are broken open and their letters spilled into a new order

explanation.surface: Genuine cases are opened to show a gardener's tools.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opened' tells you to rearrange TRUE CASES.
explanation.definitionFit: Secateurs are hand-held shears used by gardeners for pruning.

parts.note: to moderate is to alter or change
a tone is a shade of colour

explanation.surface: Someone goes white as they adjust their tone of voice.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who blanches is altering their hue, going white with shock.

clue.text: Telephoned for section of climbing equipment

explanation.surface: Someone rang about a piece of a ladder.
explanation.definitionFit: To have rung is to have phoned someone; a rung is one crossbar of a ladder.

explanation.surface: A brief part of a brawl.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrap is a small piece, and also a scuffle or brawl.

parts.note: O is the figure zero, nothing
to pen is to write

explanation.surface: A man named Frank has nothing to put down on paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like a man's name; it is the adjective meaning candid.
explanation.definitionFit: Being frank means being candid and honest, without concealment.

clue.text: Tin vessel that turned out to be a Boojum?

definitions.text: that turned out to be a Boojum?

parts.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin
an ark is a boat, like Noah's

explanation.surface: A tin boat that proved to be an imaginary monster.
explanation.walkthrough: In Lewis Carroll's poem The Hunting of the Snark, the quarry turns out to be a Boojum.
explanation.definitionFit: In Lewis Carroll's nonsense poem, the creature hunted by the crew proves to be a Boojum.

explanation.surface: A flawless singing voice.
explanation.definitionFit: Utter means complete or absolute, as in utter nonsense; to utter is to say aloud or express.

explanation.surface: A runner's side ache, with a sewing joke attached.
explanation.definitionFit: A stitch is a sharp side pain when running; a running stitch is a simple sewing stitch used to gather fabric.

clue.text: One well up in banking trials?

definitions.text: One well up in banking trials?

parts.words: One well up in banking trials?
parts.note: banking is an aircraft tilting in a turn, and well up means high in the sky, not expert in finance

explanation.surface: An expert in financial experiments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'well up in banking' suggests a financial expert; read it as flying high while tilting a plane during trials.
explanation.definitionFit: A test pilot flies new aircraft on trial flights, banking them high in the air.

parts.note: a hind is a female deer
CE stands for the Church of England

explanation.surface: A deer ran up to a church barrier.
explanation.definitionFit: A hindrance is an obstacle, something that prevents progress.

clue.text: State in which delusions rise, drunkenly?

indicators.note: staggering like a drunk, the letters of the phrase lurch into a new order

explanation.surface: A condition in which delusions come up when someone has been drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Delirium is a mental condition of confusion and wild excitement, a state of mind.

explanation.surface: A note that a standing clock, a grandfather clock, is common.
explanation.definitionFit: Face means prestige or reputation, as in losing face; 'clock' is slang for a person's visage.

clue.text: Acclaimed, Middle English is in fashion!

indicators.note: the abbreviation sits inside the word for a craze

parts.note: a fad is a passing fashion

explanation.surface: An exclamation that the medieval language is now trendy and praised.
explanation.definitionFit: Being famed means being celebrated and well known, widely praised.

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
ones are single persons or things

explanation.surface: Statues of unfeeling people.
explanation.definitionFit: Cones are three-dimensional geometric shapes with a circular base tapering to a point.

explanation.surface: A ship calls at a harbour in Panama.
explanation.definitionFit: This punctuation mark is a stop of sorts; Colón is a port at the Caribbean end of the Panama Canal.

parts.note: describes practice boxing, trading gentle punches without full force

explanation.surface: A description of gentle exchanges of punches.
explanation.definitionFit: Boxers practise in the ring by trading light punches with a partner.

clue.text: A note of music, right at a distance

parts.note: fa is the fourth note of the tonic sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A musical note heard correctly from far off.
explanation.definitionFit: Afar means far away, from or at a great distance.

clue.text: Little Mary's upset-it's the risque remarks!

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the word over so it reads bottom to top

parts.note: Little Mary is an old British euphemism for the stomach, so Little Mary's gives tums

explanation.surface: Little Mary is upset by some off-colour jokes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little Mary' looks like a girl; it is dated British slang for the stomach (from J M Barrie's play), so 'Little Mary's' is TUMS, upset to read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Smut is indecent talk or writing, the sort of off-colour jokes that shock.

clue.text: Ma is often involved in these party-promises

indicators.note: tangled up, so the letters of the three words are mixed together

explanation.surface: Mother appears often in political pledges.
explanation.definitionFit: A manifesto is a political party's published programme of pledges, so it stands for the promises collectively.

indicators.note: Piece of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Part of a firm, long fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A melon is a large fruit with sweet flesh, grown on a vine.

clue.text: Exterminator of wild reeds encircling Ilium

indicators.note: the scrambled letters wrap around the name of the ancient city
running wild, the letters of the plants scatter into a new order

parts.note: Ilium is the Latin name for Troy

explanation.surface: A killer of wild reeds surrounding the ancient city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exterminator' suggests pest control; it is a warship class. 'wild' rearranges the plants and 'encircling' wraps them round the city Homer called Ilium.
explanation.definitionFit: One who destroys or wipes out completely is an exterminator.

clue.text: Tenth article includes a little Italian

indicators.note: the article holds the abbreviation for Italian within it

parts.note: the is the definite article
IT is a short form of Italian, as in Italian vermouth

explanation.surface: A tenth of an article covers a short bit of Italian.
explanation.definitionFit: A tithe was a levy of one tenth of produce or income paid to the church.
